t: When underwriting female lives, insurers in India traditionally pay special attention to
o: Whether she has an independent income and the purpose of insurance
e: Earned-income status and insurable interest determine the sum assured allowed; housewives are usually restricted to limits linked to the husband's cover.

t: A critical illness rider typically pays a lump sum on
o: Loss of employment due to illness
Diagnosis of a listed illness after the life assured survives a specified survival period
e: The benefit is triggered by diagnosis of specified illnesses (e.g., cancer, heart attack) subject to a survival period, often 30 days.

t: Under the standard suicide clause in Indian life policies, if the life assured commits suicide within 12 months of commencement or revival, the nominee is entitled to
o: At least 80% of total premiums paid (or fund value for ULIPs)
e: The 2013/2019 product regulations mandate at least 80% of premiums paid in non-linked plans and the fund value in linked plans.

t: An 'early death claim' for investigation purposes is one arising within
o: Any time if sum assured exceeds ₹1 crore
e: Deaths within three years are investigated for possible non-disclosure, consistent with the Section 45 contestability window.

t: Under the Insurance Act 1938, the minimum paid-up equity capital required to register as a life insurer in India is
e: Section 6 of the Insurance Act prescribes a minimum paid-up equity capital of ₹100 crore for a life or general insurer.

t: Under the IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations 2024, a regular premium non-linked policy acquires a surrender value
o: Only after three full years' premiums
After payment of premium for the first policy year
e: The 2024 regulations require surrender value to be payable once the first policy year's premium has been paid.

t: If an insurer assumes a higher rate of interest in its premium calculation, other things equal, the premium will
e: A higher assumed interest rate means greater investment earnings on premiums, so a lower premium is needed to fund the same benefit.

t: A waiver of premium rider on a child plan ensures that
o: Future premiums are waived on death or disability of the proposer and the policy continues
The child need not pay premiums after age 18
e: The rider protects the savings goal by keeping the policy in force without premiums if the premium-paying parent dies or is disabled.

t: Under the IRDAI Protection of Policyholders' Interests Regulations 2024, the free-look period for a life insurance policy is
o: 30 days for all policies irrespective of mode of sale
15 days for offline and 30 days for distance marketing
e: The 2024 regulations extended free-look to 30 days from receipt of the policy document for all policies.

t: Terminal (final additional) bonus is
o: Declared every year and vested immediately
A guaranteed addition stated in the policy
A one-time bonus paid on maturity or death claims of policies that have run for a specified minimum period
e: Terminal bonus rewards long-duration policies and is not guaranteed or vested until the claim arises.

t: Under Section 39 of the Insurance Act, when a policyholder nominates his spouse, children or parents, they are treated as
o: Beneficial nominees entitled to the claim money in their own right
e: The 2015 amendment made such nominees beneficial owners of the proceeds, unlike other nominees who receive it on behalf of heirs.

t: If an insurer delays settlement of a claim beyond the regulatory timeline, it must pay interest at
e: Interest at 2% above the prevailing bank rate is payable from the date of receipt of the last necessary document.

t: The premium calculated purely from mortality and interest, before any loading for expenses, is called the
e: Net (or pure) premium covers only the expected cost of claims; adding expense and contingency loadings gives the gross or office premium.

t: A life assured dies within the days of grace with the premium unpaid. The insurer will
o: Pay the claim after deducting the unpaid premium
Reject the claim as the policy had lapsed
Pay only the premiums paid so far
e: The policy is in force during grace, so the full death benefit is payable less the outstanding premium for the policy year.

t: The First Premium Receipt (FPR) is significant because it
o: Evidences acceptance of risk and commencement of the contract
Is required for income tax purposes only
e: Issue of the FPR signifies the insurer's acceptance of the proposal; subsequent premiums are acknowledged by renewal premium receipts.

t: Following the 2022 amendment to the Corporate Agents regulations, a corporate agent such as a bank may tie up with a maximum of how many life insurers?
e: IRDAI raised the limit from three to nine insurers in each of the life, general and health categories to widen choice for customers.

t: The proposal form in life insurance constitutes
o: Acceptance of the contract by the insurer
An offer by the proposer which the insurer may accept
e: The proposer's duly filled form is the offer; the insurer's acceptance, evidenced by the first premium receipt, completes the contract.

t: A policy issued in 2024 has a sum assured of ₹3,00,000 and an annual premium of ₹40,000. The premium eligible for deduction under Section 80C is
e: Deduction is restricted to 10% of the sum assured, i.e., ₹30,000.

t: The tabular annual premium for a plan is ₹48 per ₹1,000 sum assured. For a sum assured of ₹4,00,000 with a 2% yearly-mode rebate, the premium payable is
Financial underwriting is primarily concerned with
o: Whether the sum assured is reasonable in relation to the proposer's income and insurance need
The proposer's blood pressure and BMI
e: It checks that the cover is commensurate with income and existing insurance to prevent over-insurance and speculative proposals.

t: Under a deferred annuity, the period between payment of premiums and commencement of annuity payments is the
e: During deferment the corpus accumulates; annuity payments begin after deferment at the vesting date.

t: The Agent's Confidential Report submitted with the proposal mainly helps the underwriter assess
o: Moral hazard and the proposer's background
e: The agent, having met the proposer, reports on health, habits, income and family history to supplement the proposal.

t: At vesting of a pension plan, the maximum portion of the corpus that can be commuted (taken as lump sum) under IRDAI regulations is
e: Up to 60% may be commuted and the balance must be used to buy an annuity; the commuted amount is tax-exempt under Section 10(10A).

t: Under Section 45 of the Insurance Act 1938 (as amended in 2015), a life policy cannot be called in question on any ground after
o: 2 years from the date of issue
3 years from the date of issue, revival or rider addition, whichever is later
5 years from the date of issue
It can be questioned at any time if fraud is alleged
e: After three years the policy becomes indisputable even on grounds of fraud; within three years fraud must be proved by the insurer.

t: Section 47 of the Insurance Act permits an insurer to pay the claim money into court when
o: There are conflicting claims or no clear title and the insurer cannot determine the rightful claimant
e: Payment into court discharges the insurer where it is in doubt about who is entitled to the policy moneys.

t: To issue a duplicate policy bond for a lost policy, the insurer usually requires
o: An indemnity bond, and for larger sums assured, an advertisement in a newspaper
e: The indemnity protects the insurer against claims on the original; a public advertisement is called for above specified sum assured limits.

t: Under the earlier guaranteed surrender value scale, a policy surrendered in the third policy year receives a GSV of
e: The GSV scale is 30% in the second year, 35% in the third, 50% in years four to seven and 90% in the last two years.

t: Under a limited payment whole life policy
o: Premiums are paid for a fixed number of years but cover continues for the whole of life
The sum assured is paid at age 60
The sum assured reduces after premiums stop
e: Premiums are compressed into a limited term, while the death benefit remains payable whenever death occurs.

t: A policy lapses when
o: A loan is taken on the policy
Premium remains unpaid even after expiry of the days of grace
e: Non-payment within the grace period causes lapse; benefits then depend on whether the policy has acquired paid-up status.

t: Section 41 of the Insurance Act prohibits an agent from
o: Offering a rebate of commission or premium as an inducement to take a policy
Working in more than one state
e: Rebating is an offence; the penalty under Section 41 can extend to ₹10 lakh.

t: Under the Indian Stamp Act, the stamp duty on a life insurance policy is
o: Paid by the policyholder at maturity
20 paise per ₹1,000 of sum assured, borne by the insurer
e: Life policies attract duty of 20 paise per ₹1,000 sum assured, which the insurer pays and may recover on free-look cancellation.

t: The numerical rating method of underwriting
o: Assigns debit and credit points to each risk factor to arrive at a total rating
Relies solely on the medical examiner's opinion
Is used only for group schemes
e: Each adverse factor adds debits and favourable factors give credits; the total determines standard or sub-standard classification.

t: A simple reversionary bonus declared on a participating policy
o: Is paid in cash every year
Is calculated on the sum assured and payable along with the claim
e: Simple reversionary bonus is a fixed amount per ₹1,000 sum assured added each year and paid at maturity or death.

t: A decreasing term assurance is most suitable for covering
e: The cover reduces in step with the declining loan balance, matching the liability at the lowest cost (mortgage redemption assurance).

t: The periodic payments made to the policyholder during the term of a money-back plan are called
e: Survival benefits are fixed percentages of the sum assured paid at specified intervals on the life assured surviving to those dates.

t: A proposer born on 10 May 1990 takes a policy commencing 1 January 2026. Age nearer birthday is
e: On 1 January 2026 the proposer is 35 years 7.7 months; nearer birthday rounds to 36 (age last birthday is 35).

t: A policy loan with accumulated interest exceeding the surrender value of a lapsed policy results in
o: Foreclosure of the policy by the insurer
e: When loan plus interest exceeds surrender value on a policy not in force, the insurer forecloses and the policy ceases.

t: Which statement about assignment of a life policy under Section 38 is correct?
o: Assignment automatically cancels any existing nomination except an assignment in favour of the insurer for a loan
Assignment is valid without notice to the insurer
A nomination overrides a prior assignment
e: Assignment transfers title and cancels nomination, except where the policy is assigned to the insurer as security for a policy loan.

t: The principle of underwriting that makes group term insurance cheaper than individual cover is that
o: Members are covered compulsorily or in a non-selected manner, reducing anti-selection
e: Groups formed for purposes other than insurance, with cover based on a formula, avoid adverse selection and need no individual underwriting.

t: The fund management charge in a ULIP is capped by IRDAI at
e: FMC is limited to 1.35% of fund value per annum across all fund options.

t: Under the 2019 non-linked product regulations, the revival period available to a policyholder is at least
o: 2 years from the first unpaid premium
3 years from the first unpaid premium
5 years from the first unpaid premium
Until maturity only if sum assured is below ₹1 lakh
e: Non-linked policies must allow revival within at least five years from the date of first unpaid premium (linked policies: three years).

t: A ULIP issued in June 2022 with an annual premium of ₹3,00,000 matures in 2032. Its maturity proceeds are
o: Taxable, since ULIPs issued after 1 February 2021 with premium above ₹2.5 lakh lose the exemption
Exempt because the policy ran for 10 years
Taxable only if the fund value exceeds ₹1 crore
e: Finance Act 2021 withdrew the exemption for ULIPs with aggregate premium over ₹2.5 lakh issued on or after 1 February 2021.

t: Days of grace allowed for a policy with monthly premium mode are
e: Grace is 30 days for yearly, half-yearly and quarterly modes and 15 days for the monthly mode.

t: Under IRDAI micro-insurance regulations, the maximum sum assured for an individual life micro-insurance product is
e: Micro-insurance life products are capped at ₹2 lakh sum assured and distributed through NGOs, SHGs and similar micro-insurance agents.

t: In a ULIP, the charge recovered by cancelling units every month to cover the cost of life cover is the
e: Mortality charge is the price of the sum at risk and is deducted by cancellation of units, typically monthly.

t: The minimum lock-in period for a unit-linked insurance plan is
e: IRDAI regulations fix a five-year lock-in during which no surrender proceeds or partial withdrawals can be paid.

t: A non-participating policy
o: Participates in the insurer's profits through bonus
Offers guaranteed benefits only and does not share in surplus
e: Non-par (without-profit) policies have benefits fixed at the outset; the insurer bears the full profit or loss.

t: Under an endowment assurance the sum assured is payable
o: Only on death within the term
On death during the term or on survival to the end of the term
e: Endowment combines protection and savings: the sum assured with bonuses is paid on earlier death or at maturity.

t: A Point of Sales Person (POSP) in life insurance is permitted to sell
o: Any life insurance product including ULIPs
Pre-underwritten, simple products specified by IRDAI
e: POSPs undergo minimal training and may sell only simple, standardised products where underwriting is largely automatic.

t: The Life Insurance Corporation of India commenced operations on
e: LIC was formed under the LIC Act 1956 by nationalising 245 private insurers and began operations on 1 September 1956.
